I’m digging into the SDK shape now so the plan can distinguish “supported adapter” from “would require upstream changes.”

It helps your app:\n\n- connect a user wallet signer to idOS;\n- check whether the connected wallet already has an idOS profile;\n- allow user to get encryption key from MPC nodes;\n- list and filter credentials available to the user;\n- decrypt credential content on demand;\n- create access grants so users can share credentials with consumers;\n- manage user wallets.\n\n## Installation\n\nInstall the client package:\n\n```bash\npnpm add @idos-network/client\n```\n\n## Quick architecture\n\nMost integrations follow this client state flow:\n\n1. **Configuration**: create a client with node URL and enclave options.\n2. **Idle**: runtime is ready, no wallet signer attached yet.\n3. **With user signer**: signer attached, user identity known.\n4. **Logged in**: profile fetched and enclave configured for the user.\n\nSome methods are only available in specific states. For example, `logIn()` is available after `withUserSigner(...)`, and credential operations are available after `logIn()`.\n\n## 1) Initialize the client\n\n```ts\nimport { createIDOSClient } from \"@idos-network/client\";\n\nconst idOSClientIdle = await createIDOSClient({\n  nodeUrl: \"https://nodes.idos.network\",\n  enclaveOptions: {\n    container: \"#idos-enclave\",\n  },\n}).createClient();\n```\n\n## 2) Attach the user signer\n\nUse your app's wallet integration (for example, ethers) and attach the signer:\n\n```ts\nimport { ethers } from \"ethers\";\n\nconst provider = new ethers.BrowserProvider(window.ethereum);\nawait provider.send(\"eth_requestAccounts\", []);\nconst signer = await provider.getSigner();\n\nconst idOSClientWithSigner = await idOSClientIdle.withUserSigner(signer);\n```\n\n## 3) Check profile and log in\n\nOnce the signer is attached, check if the user has an idOS profile and then log them in:\n\n```ts\nconst hasProfile = await idOSClientWithSigner.hasProfile();\n\nif (!hasProfile) {\n  // Redirect to your onboarding/profile-creation flow.\n}\n\nconst idOSClientLoggedIn = await idOSClientWithSigner.logIn();\n```\n\nAfter login, `idOSClientLoggedIn.user` contains user metadata from idOS.\n\n## 4) Read and filter credentials\n\n### List all credential headers\n\n```ts\nconst credentials = await idOSClientLoggedIn.getAllCredentials();\n```\n\nThis returns list items (metadata/public notes), not decrypted private content.\n\n### Filter credentials by issuer, level, and fields\n\n```ts\nconst filtered = await idOSClientLoggedIn.filterCredentials({\n  acceptedIssuers: [{ authPublicKey: \"ISSUER_AUTH_PUBLIC_KEY_HEX\" }],\n  credentialLevelOrHigherFilter: {\n    userLevel: \"basic\",\n    requiredAddons: [\"email\", \"liveness\"],\n  },\n  publicNotesFieldFilters: {\n    pick: { type: [\"human\"] },\n    omit: {},\n  },\n});\n```\n\n### Read private content for a specific credential\n\n```ts\nconst content = await idOSClientLoggedIn.getCredentialContent(\"CREDENTIAL_ID\");\nconst contentHash = await idOSClientLoggedIn.getCredentialContentSha256Hash(\"CREDENTIAL_ID\");\n```\n\nThe SDK decrypts through the enclave provider, so plaintext handling stays in the user session context.\n\n## 5) Share a credential (request access grant)\n\nTo share a credential with a consumer app/service, create an access grant:\n\n```ts\nconst grant = await idOSClientLoggedIn.requestAccessGrant(\"CREDENTIAL_ID\", {\n  consumerAuthPublicKey: \"CONSUMER_AUTH_PUBLIC_KEY_HEX\",\n  consumerEncryptionPublicKey: \"CONSUMER_ENCRYPTION_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64\",\n  lockedUntil: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 90 * 24 * 60 * 60, // optional\n});\n```\n\n`requestAccessGrant(...)` creates a shared credential copy encrypted for the consumer and returns the created grant payload.\n\n## 6) Manage wallets\n\nAdd a wallet:\n\n```ts\nawait idOSClientLoggedIn.addWallet({\n  id: crypto.randomUUID(),\n  address: \"0x...\",\n  public_key: \"0x...\",\n  message: \"Sign this message to prove wallet ownership\",\n  signature: \"0x...\",\n  wallet_type: \"EVM\",\n});\n```\n\nList and remove wallets:\n\n```ts\nconst wallets = await idOSClientLoggedIn.getWallets();\nawait idOSClientLoggedIn.removeWallet(wallets[0].id);\n```\n\n`wallet_type` must match one of the supported chains (for example `EVM`, `NEAR`, `XRPL`, `STELLAR`).\n\n## Optional: onboarding helper for profile creation\n\nIf your product includes profile creation, the client SDK can generate the encryption profile that your backend/issuer flow needs:\n\n```ts\nconst encryptionProfile = await idOSClientWithSigner.createUserEncryptionProfile(\"USER_UUID\");\n```\n\nThen pass `encryptionProfile` and wallet ownership proof to your backend service that performs user creation in idOS.\n\n## Optional: request a delegated write grant signature\n\nIf an issuer integration needs user consent for delegated writes, ask the user to sign a DWG message:\n\n```ts\nconst delegatedWriteGrant = {\n access_grant_timelock: new Date().toISOString().replace(/\\.\\d+Z$/g, \"Z\"),\n  not_usable_before: new Date().toISOString().replace(/\\.\\d+Z$/g, \"Z\"),\n  not_usable_after: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)\n    .toISOString()\n    .replace(/\\.\\d+Z$/g, \"Z\"),\n};\n\nconst message = await idOSClientLoggedIn.requestDWGMessage(delegatedWriteGrant);\nconst signature = await signer.signMessage(message);\n```\n\nYour backend/issuer service can then submit this grant and signature when writing credentials on behalf of the user.\n\n## Logout\n\n```ts\nconst idOSClientIdleAgain = await idOSClientLoggedIn.logOut();\n```\n",

It helps your app:\n\n- connect a user wallet signer to idOS;\n- check whether the connected wallet already has an idOS profile;\n- allow user to get encryption key from MPC nodes;\n- list and filter credentials available to the user;\n- decrypt credential content on demand;\n- create access grants so users can share credentials with consumers;\n- manage user wallets.\n\n## Installation\n\nInstall the client package:\n\n```bash\npnpm add @idos-network/client\n```\n\n## Quick architecture\n\nMost integrations follow this client state flow:\n\n1. **Configuration**: create a client with node URL and enclave options.\n2. **Idle**: runtime is ready, no wallet signer attached yet.\n3. **With user signer**: signer attached, user identity known.\n4. **Logged in**: profile fetched and enclave configured for the user.\n\nSome methods are only available in specific states. For example, `logIn()` is available after `withUserSigner(...)`, and credential operations are available after `logIn()`.\n\n## 1) Initialize the client\n\n```ts\nimport { createIDOSClient } from \"@idos-network/client\";\n\nconst idOSClientIdle = await createIDOSClient({\n  nodeUrl: \"https://nodes.idos.network\",\n  enclaveOptions: {\n    container: \"#idos-enclave\",\n  },\n}).createClient();\n```\n\n## 2) Attach the user signer\n\nUse your app's wallet integration (for example, ethers) and attach the signer:\n\n```ts\nimport { ethers } from \"ethers\";\n\nconst provider = new ethers.BrowserProvider(window.ethereum);\nawait provider.send(\"eth_requestAccounts\", []);\nconst signer = await provider.getSigner();\n\nconst idOSClientWithSigner = await idOSClientIdle.withUserSigner(signer);\n```\n\n## 3) Check profile and log in\n\nOnce the signer is attached, check if the user has an idOS profile and then log them in:\n\n```ts\nconst hasProfile = await idOSClientWithSigner.hasProfile();\n\nif (!hasProfile) {\n  // Redirect to your onboarding/profile-creation flow.\n}\n\nconst idOSClientLoggedIn = await idOSClientWithSigner.logIn();\n```\n\nAfter login, `idOSClientLoggedIn.user` contains user metadata from idOS.\n\n## 4) Read and filter credentials\n\n### List all credential headers\n\n```ts\nconst credentials = await idOSClientLoggedIn.getAllCredentials();\n```\n\nThis returns list items (metadata/public notes), not decrypted private content.\n\n### Filter credentials by issuer, level, and fields\n\n```ts\nconst filtered = await idOSClientLoggedIn.filterCredentials({\n  acceptedIssuers: [{ authPublicKey: \"ISSUER_AUTH_PUBLIC_KEY_HEX\" }],\n  credentialLevelOrHigherFilter: {\n {

    {
      "type": "read",
      "cmd": "sed -n '1,240p' /tmp/idos-sdk-js/docs/guide-issuer.md",

  "source": "unified_exec_startup",
  "stdout": "# Issuer Guide\n\n## Required reading\n\n- [idOS System Overview](README.md)\n- [The idOS Enclave](enclave.md)\n\n## SDK feature overview\n\nThe primary features provided by the Issuer SDK are:\n\n- checking if your user has an idOS profile, and create one otherwise;\n- transforming IDV results into idOS credentials;\n- issuing and managing credentials through standard idOS sharing primitives.\n\n## Getting started: what you'll need\n\n### Compliance guidance\n\nSee [idOS Regulatory approach](https://docs.idos.network/compliance/idos-regulatory-approach) for more context, and discuss with your compliance officer:\n\n- what retention and credential-sharing policies your issuance flow needs to support.\n\n### Signature and encryption keys\n\n> 🛑 DANGER 🛑\n>\n> Make sure you don't lose access to either secret keys. Otherwise, you won't be able to authenticate or decrypt credential contents. The idOS team won't be able to help you.\n\nYou'll need:\n\n- `encryptionSecretKey`: base64-encoded `nacl.BoxKeyPair` secret key. It'll be used to encrypt the credentials you issue to your users\n  - see [Encryption](encryption.md) for more information\n- `signingKeyPair`: this can be a NEAR `KeyPair`, a `nacl.SignKeyPair`, or an `ethers.Wallet`. This will be used to sign RPC calls to the idOS nodes.\n  - see [Signatures](signatures.md) for more information\n\nYou'll also need a `multibaseSigningKeyPair`, which will be used to sign the W3C VCs you issue. If you're unfamiliar with how to generate one, you can use the following example:\n\n```js\nimport { Ed25519VerificationKey2020 } from \"https://esm.sh/@digitalcredentials/ed25519-verification-key-2020\";\n\nconst key = await Ed25519VerificationKey2020.generate();\nconsole.log(key.privateKeyMultibase); // -> z...  (multibase, multicodec-prefixed)\nconsole.log(key.publicKeyMultibase);\n```\n\n### A frontend\n\nYour frontend (web or native app), as your user’s touch point, is where you’ll:\n\n- confirm that the user is in idOS;\n- find whether the user already has your credential;\n- otherwise, request write grant and take user through IDV.\n\n### A backend\n\nYour backend (private server) is where you’ll:\n\n- create user profiles in idOS;\n- write credentials to idOS;\n- revoking previously issued credentials.\n\n### Our Issuer SDK\n\nGet our NPM packages\n\n- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@idos-network/client\n- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@idos-network/issuer\n\nand their dependencies with pnpm (or your package manager of choice)\n\n```\npnpm add @idos-network/client\npnpm add @idos-network/issuer\n```\n\n## Usage\n\n### [ frontend ] Importing and initializing\n\n```js\nimport { createIDOSClient, type idOSClient } from \"@idos-network/client\";\n\nconst idOSClient = createIDOSClient({\n  enclaveOptions: {\n    container: \"#idOS-enclave\",\n  },\n});\n```\n\n### [ backend ] Importing and initializing\n\n```js\nimport { idOSIssuer as idOSIssuerClass } from \"@idos-network/issuer\";\n\nconst idOSIssuer = await idOSIssuerClass.init({\n  nodeUrl: KWIL_NODE_URL,\n  signingKeyPair: nacl.sign.keyPair.fromSecretKey(decode(ISSUER_SIGNING_SECRET_KEY)),\n  encryptionSecretKey: decode(ISSUER_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY),\n});\n```\n\n### [ frontend ] Connecting your user's wallet\n\nConnect your user's wallet however you do it today, for example:\n\n```js\nconst provider = new ethers.BrowserProvider(window.ethereum);\nawait provider.send(\"eth_requestAccounts\", []);\nconst signer = await provider.getSigner();\n```\n\n### [ frontend + backend ] Ensuring your user has an idOS profile\n\nGet your user's address from the signer above and confirm they have an idOS profile. If not, redirect them to your onboarding journey.\n\n```js\nconst address = await signer.getAddress();\nconst hasProfile = await idOSClient.addressHasProfile(address);\n\nif (!hasProfile) window.location = \"https://kyc-provider.example.com/enroll\";\n```\n\n#### Creating a profile\n\nIf they don't have a profile, you must create one for them. This procedure can only be done by a Permissioned Issuer. If you're interested in being one: securely generate an `ed25516` signing key, grab its public key in hex, and get in touch with us at engineering@idos.network.\n\nTo create a user profile in idOS, you need:\n\n1. **A wallet address** associated with the user.\n2. **A public encryption key** derived from either a password chosen by the user in the idOS enclave app.\n\n##### Step 1: Deciding on a user id\n\nDeciding on a user id for a user is an issuer decision. You can use whichever you want, as long as it's an [UUID](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universally_unique_identifier).\n\n```js\n// backend\n\nconst userId = crypto.randomUUID();\n\n// Remember it on your database\n// e.g. session.user.update({ userId });\n\n// Return it to the front-end to be used in the next step\nreturn { userId };\n```\n\n##### Step 2: Getting the user's signing and encryption public keys\n\nUse the `idOSClient.createUserEncryptionProfile` function to derive a public key for the user. This key will be used to encrypt and decrypt user's credential content.\n\n```javascript\n// frontend\n\nconst encryptionProfile = await idOSClient.createUserEncryptionProfile(userId);\n\nconst ownershipProofMessage = \"Please sign this message to confirm you own this wallet address\";\n\nconst ownershipProofSignature = await ethereum.request({\n  method: \"personal_sign\",\n  params: [ownershipProofMessage, address],\n});\n\n// Report it back to your server\n// e.g. await yourServer.report(encryptionProfile, ownershipProofSignature);\n```\n\n##### Step 3: Creating a User Profile\n\nOnce the public key is derived, you can create the user profile in idOS by passing it to the `createUser` function alongside with user id and the wallet the user's going to use to drive their idOS profile.\n\n```javascript\n// backend\n\nconst user = {\n  id: userId,\n  recipient_encryption_public_key: encryptionProfile.userEncryptionPublicKey,\n  encryption_password_store: encryptionProfile.encryptionPasswordStore,\n};\n\nconst wallet = {\n  address,\n  wallet_type: \"EVM\", // Options: \"EVM\", \"NEAR\", \"XRPL\", \"STELLAR\"\n  message: ownershipProofMessage,\n  signature: ownershipProofSignature,\n  public_key: ethers.SigningKey.recoverPublicKey(\n    ethers.id(ownershipProofMessage),\n    ownershipProofSignature,\n  ),\n};\n\nawait idOSIssuer.createUser(user, wallet);\n```\n\n### [ frontend ] Setting signer\n\nPass your user’s signer to the SDK, so it knows where to send signature requests to.\n\n```js\nidOSClient = await idOSClient.withUserSigner(signer);\n```\n\n### [ frontend ] Checking for issued credential\n\n```typescript\nconst credentials: IdosCredential[] = await idOSClient.getAllCredentials();\n\ncredentials.filter(\n  (c) =>\n    c.issuer_auth_public_key === signingKeyPair.publicKey &&\n    JSON.parse(c.public_notes).type === \"super-kyc\",\n);\n```\n\nIf ## Assistant

I’ve got enough to draft a meaningful plan. One important constraint emerged: a real end-to-end idOS login is not just “plug in a signer” if the profile doesn’t already exist, because profile creation is issuer-gated in idOS. I’m now framing the plan around two tracks: a pure signer-auth spike, and the minimum viable path to get a real profile attached to that signer.

## Assistant

I can read both doc sites.

What I learned: Canton external parties are a good fit for this experiment. The core model is that the party owns its submission key(s), the participant prepares the transaction, and the party explicitly signs the transaction hash before execution. Digital Asset’s Wallet SDK also gives us a TypeScript path for Ed25519 key generation and external-party allocation, which is better than starting from the lower-level Python tutorials for this repo.

The main wrinkle is on the idOS side. The public docs emphasize EVM and NEAR for user login, and say generic Ed25519 is for issuers. But the current `idos-sdk-js` source is a bit ahead of the website docs: it has broader wallet types plus a custom signer path and raw Ed25519 verification for `FaceSign`-style signers. So the idea is plausible, but the cleanest path is an SDK-source-backed experiment rather than something explicitly documented as a first-class public flow. The bigger blocker is bootstrap: a real idOS profile must already exist for that signer, or be created by a permissioned issuer.

**Plan Draft**
1. Start greenfield with a TypeScript demo app, since both ecosystems give us workable JS/TS SDK surfaces.
2. Build a small Canton key module that generates or imports one Ed25519 keypair, derives the Canton public key/fingerprint/party info, and can sign Canton transaction hashes.
3. Build an idOS signer adapter around that same keypair. First attempt: use the current idOS custom/`FaceSign`-style Ed25519 path. Fallback: emulate the documented NEAR-style Ed25519 auth flow if the first path hits a real network constraint.
4. Build the trivial UI:
   - Generate or load Canton signer
   - Show Canton public key and derived identity info
   - Run `idOS.hasProfile(...)`
   - If profile exists, log in and show minimal idOS user/profile state
   - If profile does not exist, show the exact onboarding gap instead of hiding it
5. Add one Canton proof-of-life action so the signer is not only “idOS-compatible” but demonstrably Canton-compatible too. For v1 this can be signing a prepared Canton hash; full ledger submission can be the next step.
6. If you want real end-to-end login on a fresh signer, add a second track for idOS bootstrap via a permissioned issuer or an existing profile creation flow.

My recommendation is to treat v1 as “same Ed25519 keypair, two adapters, real idOS login if a profile already exists.” That isolates the cross-system signer question first, which is the real experiment.

What I need from you before I start implementing:
1. Do you want the first spike to assume an existing idOS profile for the signer, or do you want me to solve profile creation too?
2. Do you already have a Canton dev/localnet in mind, or should I optimize for a repo-local demo using the Wallet SDK first?
3. Are you comfortable using one Ed25519 keypair for both Canton and idOS in the prototype, even though Canton recommends separate keys in production?

## User

The docs are wrong. app.idos.network has a faceisgn button.

## Assistant

I’m treating the public docs as stale and the repo/application behavior as the source of truth. The codebase backs you up: idOS’s dashboard ships a FaceSign entrypoint and its backend creates profiles with `wallet_type: "FaceSign"`. ## Assistant

There’s one non-obvious integration risk I need to factor in: FaceSign itself is embeddable through a separate enclave service, and that service has an allowed-origins gate. So FaceSign is valid for bootstrap, but using it from our own localhost app may or may not work without additional access. I’m checking the enclave’s origin policy now so the plan doesn’t assume a bootstrap path we can’t actually run.

## Assistant

You’re right. I’ll treat the app and SDK source as the source of truth on FaceSign, not the public docs.

**Revised Plan**
1. Build this as a repo-local TypeScript demo, with no Daml and no smart-contract work.
2. Use the Canton Wallet SDK for the Canton side so the signer is genuinely shaped like a Canton external-party signer flow, not just a random Ed25519 key.
3. Expose that same Ed25519 key to idOS through a custom signer adapter. The current idOS SDK can accept custom signers, and the current `FaceSign` verification path is raw Ed25519 over a hex public key, which is the bridge we can exploit for the PoC.
4. First milestone: prove login works with the Canton signer, assuming the signer is already linked to an idOS profile.
5. Second milestone: handle bootstrap/linking. Best case, we automate it with FaceSign. Fallback, we use `app.idos.network` for the one-time FaceSign bootstrap and keep our local app focused on the Canton-sign-in flow.
6. Demo flow:
   - create/load one Ed25519 signer
   - show Canton key info
   - show an idOS adapter view of that same key
   - check `hasProfile()`
   - if linked, `logIn()` to idOS
   - show the same user/profile plus wallet list
   - show a Canton signing proof with the same key

**Important Constraint**
The one real uncertainty is bootstrap automation. FaceSign is live, but using it from our own app may depend on idOS origin/issuer setup. So I want to structure the work so that the core experiment, “can one Canton signer log into idOS?”, does not depend on solving that first.

If that framing matches what you want, I’ll start scaffolding the app and implement milestone 1 first.

**References**
- https://docs.digitalasset.com/integrate/devnet/party-management/index.html
- https://docs.digitalasset.com/integrate/devnet/preparing-and-signing-transactions/index.html
- https://github.com/idos-network/idos-sdk-js/blob/main/packages/kwil-infra/src/create-kwil-signer.ts
- https://github.com/idos-network/idos-sdk-js/blob/main/packages/kwil-infra/src/signature-verification/index.ts

# BACKLOG

## Goal

Prove that a single Ed25519 signer can be shared between:

- Canton external-party signing flows
- idOS user authentication flows

This repo is intentionally PoC quality. No Daml work for now. Focus on signer reuse.

## Working assumptions

- Source of truth for idOS capabilities is the current app and SDK behavior, not the public docs.
- FaceSign exists and can create/link idOS profiles, but embedding it from our own app may depend on origin and issuer setup.
- For the PoC, one Ed25519 keypair may be reused across both systems.
- Canton-side account abstraction is explicitly out of scope for v1.

## Milestone 1: Shared signer spike

- [ ] Initialize a TypeScript app in this repo
- [ ] Add a minimal local app shell for the demo
- [ ] Integrate Canton Wallet SDK
- [ ] Implement Ed25519 key generation/load for the Canton signer
- [ ] Implement a Canton signer module that can:
  - [ ] expose public key and derived identifiers
  - [ ] sign Canton transaction hashes
- [ ] Implement an idOS signer adapter backed by the same Ed25519 key
- [ ] Validate which idOS wallet path is the right bridge for the PoC:
  - [ ] custom signer
  - [ ] `FaceSign`-style raw Ed25519 path
- [ ] Build demo UI flow:
  - [ ] create/load signer
  - [ ] show signer public key and metadata
  - [ ] check idOS profile existence
  - [ ] if linked, log in to idOS
  - [ ] show basic idOS profile state
  - [ ] show Canton signing proof
- [ ] Add basic smoke tests or scripted verification where practical

## Milestone 2: Bootstrap/linking

- [ ] Determine whether our local app can embed FaceSign directly
- [ ] If yes, implement one-time profile creation/link flow in-repo
- [ ] If no, document the manual bootstrap via `app.idos.network`
- [ ] Verify that a profile created or linked through FaceSign can later be used by the shared Canton signer flow

## Milestone 3: Cleanup

- [ ] Document local setup and required env vars
- [ ] Document exact limits and known shortcuts in the PoC
- [ ] Capture follow-up work for productionizing the approach

## Open questions

- [ ] Does idOS accept the shared signer cleanly through the current custom-signer path, or do we need to present it specifically as `FaceSign`?
- [ ] What is the minimum Canton setup needed to demonstrate signer legitimacy without pulling in unnecessary network complexity?
- [ ] Can FaceSign bootstrap be exercised from localhost, or only from idOS-controlled origins?

## Not doing now

- [ ] Daml models or contracts
- [ ] Canton account abstraction
- [ ] Production key isolation
- [ ] Full UX polish

  );
}

const hexAlphabet = "0123456789abcdef";

export function bytesToHex(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  let result = "";

  for (const byte of bytes) {
    result += hexAlphabet[byte >> 4] + hexAlphabet[byte & 0x0f];
  }

  return result;
}

export function hexToBytes(hex: string): Uint8Array {
  if (hex.length % 2 !== 0) {
    throw new Error("Hex string must have an even length.");
  }

  const bytes = new Uint8Array(hex.length / 2);

  for (let index = 0; index < hex.length; index += 2) {
    bytes[index / 2] = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(index, index + 2), 16);
  }

  return bytes;
}

export function bytesToBase64(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  let binary = "";

  for (const byte of bytes) {
    binary += String.fromCharCode(byte);
  }

  return btoa(binary);
}

export function base64ToBytes(value: string): Uint8Array {
  const binary = atob(value);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);

  for (let index = 0; index < binary.length; index += 1) {
    bytes[index] = binary.charCodeAt(index);
  }

  return bytes;
}

import { getPublicKeyFromPrivate, signTransactionHash } from "@canton-network/wallet-sdk";
import nacl from "tweetnacl";

import { base64ToBytes, bytesToBase64, bytesToHex } from "./bytes";

const STORAGE_KEY = "experiment-canton:shared-signer";
const SAMPLE_CANTON_HASH = "11".repeat(32);
const SAMPLE_IDOS_MESSAGE = "idOS authentication";

export type SharedSignerRecord = {
  privateKeyBase64: string;
};

export type SharedSignerSnapshot = {
  privateKeyBase64: string;
  cantonPublicKeyBase64: string;
  ed25519PublicKeyHex: string;
  idosAdapter: {
    publicAddress: string;
    publicKey: string;
    signatureType: "ed25519";
    walletType: "FaceSign";
  };
  sample: {
    cantonHashHex: string;
    cantonSignatureBase64: string;
    idosMessage: string;
    idosSignatureHex: string;
  };
};

function createSignerRecord(): SharedSignerRecord {
  const keyPair = nacl.sign.keyPair();

  return {
    privateKeyBase64: bytesToBase64(keyPair.secretKey),
  };
}

function readStoredSigner(): SharedSignerRecord | null {
  const rawValue = window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);

  if (!rawValue) {
    return null;
  }

  const parsed = JSON.parse(rawValue) as Partial<SharedSignerRecord>;

  if (!parsed.privateKeyBase64) {
    return null;
  }

  return {
    privateKeyBase64: parsed.privateKeyBase64,
  };
}

function persistSigner(record: SharedSignerRecord): void {
  window.localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(record));
}

function toIdosSignature(privateKeyBase64: string, message: string): string {
  const signature = nacl.sign.detached(
    new TextEncoder().encode(message),
    base64ToBytes(privateKeyBase64),
  );

  return bytesToHex(signature);
}

export function loadOrCreateSharedSigner(forceNew = false): SharedSignerSnapshot {
  const record = forceNew ? createSignerRecord() : (readStoredSigner() ?? createSignerRecord());
  persistSigner(record);

  const cantonPublicKeyBase64 = getPublicKeyFromPrivate(record.privateKeyBase64);
  const ed25519PublicKeyHex = bytesToHex(base64ToBytes(cantonPublicKeyBase64));

  return {
    privateKeyBase64: record.privateKeyBase64,
    cantonPublicKeyBase64,
    ed25519PublicKeyHex,
    idosAdapter: {
      publicAddress: ed25519PublicKeyHex,
      publicKey: ed25519PublicKeyHex,
      signatureType: "ed25519",
      walletType: "FaceSign",
    },
    sample: {
      cantonHashHex: SAMPLE_CANTON_HASH,
      cantonSignatureBase64: signTransactionHash(SAMPLE_CANTON_HASH, record.privateKeyBase64),
      idosMessage: SAMPLE_IDOS_MESSAGE,
      idosSignatureHex: toIdosSignature(record.privateKeyBase64, SAMPLE_IDOS_MESSAGE),
    },
  };
}

import { type KwilSigner, type Types, Utils, WebKwil } from "@kwilteam/kwil-js";

type CreateKwilClientParams = {
  chainId?: string;
  nodeUrl: string;
};

const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;

const actionSchema = {
  get_user: [],
  has_profile: [
    {
      name: "address",
      type: Utils.DataType.Text,
    },
  ],
} as const;

type ActionName = keyof typeof actionSchema;
type PositionalParams = Types.PositionalParams;

type CallParams<Name extends ActionName> = {
  name: Name;
  inputs: Record<(typeof actionSchema)[Name][number]["name"], unknown>;
};

export class KwilActionClient {
  signer?: KwilSigner;
  readonly client: WebKwil;
  readonly chainId: string;

  constructor(client: WebKwil, chainId: string) {
    this.client = client;
    this.chainId = chainId;
  }

  private createActionInputs(actionName: ActionName, params: Record<string, unknown>): PositionalParams {
    if (!Object.keys(params).length) {
      return [];
    }

    return actionSchema[actionName].map(({ name }) => {
      const value = params[name];

      if (value === "" || value === 0) {
        return value;
      }

      return value ?? null;
    }) as PositionalParams;
  }

  private actionTypes(actionName: ActionName) {
    return actionSchema[actionName].map((entry) => entry.type);
  }

  async call<T>(params: CallParams<ActionName>, signer: KwilSigner | undefined = this.signer): Promise<T> {
    const action = {
      name: params.name,
      namespace: "main",
      inputs: this.createActionInputs(params.name, params.inputs),
      types: this.actionTypes(params.name),
    };

    const response = await this.client.call(action, signer);
    return response?.data?.result as T;
  }

  setSigner(signer: KwilSigner | undefined): void {
    this.signer = signer;
  }
}

export async function createWebKwilClient({
  chainId,
  nodeUrl,
}: CreateKwilClientParams): Promise<KwilActionClient> {
  const discoveryClient = new WebKwil({ kwilProvider: nodeUrl, chainId: "" });
  const discoveredChainId =
    chainId ?? (await discoveryClient.chainInfo({ disableWarning: true })).data?.chain_id;

  if (!discoveredChainId) {
    throw new Error("Unable to discover the idOS chain ID.");
  }

  return new KwilActionClient(
    new WebKwil({
      kwilProvider: nodeUrl,
      chainId: discoveredChainId,
      timeout: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS,
    }),
    discoveredChainId,
  );
}

import type { KwilSigner } from "@kwilteam/kwil-js";

import type { KwilActionClient } from "./kwilActionClient";

export type IdosUser = {
  id: string;
  recipient_encryption_public_key: string;
  encryption_password_store: "user" | "mpc";
};

export async function hasProfile(kwilClient: KwilActionClient, address: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const result = await kwilClient.call<{ has_profile: boolean }[]>({
    name: "has_profile",
    inputs: { address },
  });

  return Boolean(result[0]?.has_profile);
}

export async function getUser(
  kwilClient: KwilActionClient,
  signer: KwilSigner | undefined = kwilClient.signer,
): Promise<IdosUser | null> {
  const result = await kwilClient.call<IdosUser[]>(
    {
      name: "get_user",
      inputs: {},
    },
    signer,
  );

  return result[0] ?? null;
}

import { KwilSigner } from "@kwilteam/kwil-js";

import type { SharedSignerSnapshot } from "../sharedSigner";
import { hexToBytes } from "../bytes";
import { signDetachedMessage } from "../sharedSigner";
import { getUser, hasProfile, type IdosUser } from "./actions";
import { createWebKwilClient } from "./kwilActionClient";

const DEFAULT_IDOS_NODE_URL = "https://nodes.idos.network";

export type IdosInspectorResult = {
  nodeUrl: string;
  chainId: string;
  address: string;
  hasProfile: boolean;
  user: IdosUser | null;
};

function createIdosKwilSigner(snapshot: SharedSignerSnapshot): KwilSigner {
  return new KwilSigner(
    async (message: Uint8Array) => signDetachedMessage(snapshot.privateKeyBase64, message),
    hexToBytes(snapshot.ed25519PublicKeyHex),
    "ed25519",
  );
}

export async function inspectIdosSigner(
  snapshot: SharedSignerSnapshot,
  nodeUrl = DEFAULT_IDOS_NODE_URL,
): Promise<IdosInspectorResult> {
  const kwilClient = await createWebKwilClient({ nodeUrl });
  const signer = createIdosKwilSigner(snapshot);

  kwilClient.setSigner(signer);

  const profileExists = await hasProfile(kwilClient, snapshot.idosAdapter.publicAddress);
  const user = profileExists ? await getUser(kwilClient, signer) : null;

  return {
    nodeUrl,
    chainId: kwilClient.chainId,
    address: snapshot.idosAdapter.publicAddress,
    hasProfile: profileExists,
    user,
  };
}

## User

I'm a bit lost. How can I add a key generated in the UI to my idOS profile?

## Assistant

The short answer: you currently can’t do that through the FaceSign button.

What we have in [sharedSigner.ts](/Users/pkoch/github.com/idos-network/experiment-canton/src/lib/sharedSigner.ts) is a local browser-generated Ed25519 key. Right now it lives only in your browser `localStorage`. idOS does not know about it until we explicitly register it.

There are only two realistic ways to attach that key to an idOS profile:

1. If you already have an idOS profile:
   Log in with an existing linked wallet, then call idOS `add_wallet` for the generated key.
   The payload would be roughly:
   - `address`: generated public key hex
   - `public_key`: same public key hex
   - `wallet_type`: `FaceSign` for the current raw-Ed25519 path
   - `message`: proof-of-ownership message
   - `signature`: Ed25519 signature from the generated key over that message

2. If you do not already have an idOS profile:
   A permissioned issuer has to create the profile with that key as the initial wallet.
   FaceSign bootstrap does not import our key. It creates and uses its own FaceSign-managed key.

So the blocker is not “how do you click the right button”; it’s that FaceSign is a separate signer system, not a bring-your-own-key import flow.

The practical next move is:
I build a “log in with your existing idOS wallet, then link the generated key” flow. That would let you keep the shared UI-generated key and attach it to your current profile. If you want, I’ll do that next.

## Assistant

I’m making the core edits now: EVM connector, `add_wallet` execution, and a UI section that stops exactly at the point where you need to sign with your existing wallet. After that I’ll run a build and, if possible, a non-browser smoke check against the live node.

## User (checkpoint)

When adding the ed25519 signer to the idOS profile that the user connects to, add it as a NEAR wallet with its implicit address to keep things simple.

## Assistant

I’m switching the linking design to NEAR-style Ed25519, per your note. First I’m verifying the worktree is still clean after the interrupted turn, then I’ll wire a generated NEP-413 proof so the browser-generated key can be added as a `NEAR` wallet using its implicit address.

export type ExistingWalletInspection = {
  address: string;
  chainId: string;
  hasProfile: boolean;
  nodeUrl: string;
  user: IdosUser | null;
  wallets: IdosWallet[];
};

export type LinkGeneratedSignerResult = {
  txHash?: string;
  inspection: ExistingWalletInspection;
  status: "linked" | "already-linked";
};

function createIdosKwilSigner(snapshot: SharedSignerSnapshot): KwilSigner {
  return new KwilSigner(
    async (message: Uint8Array) =>
      signNearMessage({
        privateKeyBase64: snapshot.privateKeyBase64,
        message: new TextDecoder().decode(message),
      }),
    hexToBytes(snapshot.ed25519PublicKeyHex),
    "nep413",
  );

}

function createEvmKwilSigner(signer: JsonRpcSigner, address: string): KwilSigner {
  return new KwilSigner(signer, address);
}

export async function inspectExistingWallet(
  signer: JsonRpcSigner,
  address: string,
  nodeUrl = DEFAULT_IDOS_NODE_URL,
): Promise<ExistingWalletInspection> {
  const kwilClient = await createWebKwilClient({ nodeUrl });
  const kwilSigner = createEvmKwilSigner(signer, address);
  kwilClient.setSigner(kwilSigner);

  const profileExists = await hasProfile(kwilClient, address);
  const user = profileExists ? await getUser(kwilClient, kwilSigner) : null;
  const wallets = profileExists ? await getWallets(kwilClient, kwilSigner) : [];

  return {
    address,
    chainId: kwilClient.chainId,
    hasProfile: profileExists,
    nodeUrl,
    user,
    wallets,
  };
}

export async function linkGeneratedNearWalletToExistingProfile({
  existingWalletAddress,
  existingWalletSigner,
  snapshot,
  nodeUrl = DEFAULT_IDOS_NODE_URL,
}: {
  existingWalletAddress: string;
  existingWalletSigner: JsonRpcSigner;
  snapshot: SharedSignerSnapshot;
  nodeUrl?: string;
}): Promise<LinkGeneratedSignerResult> {
  const kwilClient = await createWebKwilClient({ nodeUrl });
  const kwilSigner = createEvmKwilSigner(existingWalletSigner, existingWalletAddress);
  kwilClient.setSigner(kwilSigner);

  const profileExists = await hasProfile(kwilClient, existingWalletAddress);
  if (!profileExists) {
    throw new Error("The connected EVM wallet does not have an idOS profile.");
  }

  const walletsBefore = await getWallets(kwilClient, kwilSigner);
  const alreadyLinked = walletsBefore.some(
    (wallet) =>
      wallet.address === snapshot.idosAdapter.publicAddress &&
      wallet.wallet_type === snapshot.idosAdapter.walletType,
  );

  if (alreadyLinked) {
    return {
      status: "already-linked",
      inspection: await inspectExistingWallet(existingWalletSigner, existingWalletAddress, nodeUrl),
    };
  }

  const message = `Link this generated Canton signer to my idOS profile. Nonce ${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
  const signatureBytes = await signNearMessage({
    privateKeyBase64: snapshot.privateKeyBase64,
    message,
  });
  const txHash = await addWallet(
    kwilClient,
    {
      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
      address: snapshot.idosAdapter.publicAddress,
      public_key: snapshot.idosAdapter.publicKey,
      wallet_type: "NEAR",
      message,
      signature: Array.from(signatureBytes, (byte) => byte.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join(""),
    },
    kwilSigner,
  );

  return {
    txHash,
    status: "linked",
    inspection: await inspectExistingWallet(existingWalletSigner, existingWalletAddress, nodeUrl),
  };
}

import { BrowserProvider, type JsonRpcSigner } from "ethers";

export type ConnectedEvmWallet = {
  address: string;
  signer: JsonRpcSigner;
};

export async function connectEvmWallet(): Promise<ConnectedEvmWallet> {
  if (!("ethereum" in window)) {
    throw new Error("No injected EVM wallet was found in this browser.");
  }

  const provider = new BrowserProvider(window.ethereum);
  await provider.send("eth_requestAccounts", []);

  const signer = await provider.getSigner();
  const address = await signer.getAddress();

  return {
    address,
    signer,
  };
}

}

export function concatBytes(...values: Uint8Array[]): Uint8Array {
  const totalLength = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value.length, 0);
  const result = new Uint8Array(totalLength);

  let offset = 0;

  for (const value of values) {
    result.set(value, offset);
    offset += value.length;
  }

  return result;
}

export function uint16ToBigEndian(value: number): Uint8Array {
  return new Uint8Array([(value >> 8) & 0xff, value & 0xff]);
}

import { serialize } from "borsh";
import bs58 from "bs58";

import { concatBytes, uint16ToBigEndian } from "./bytes";
import { signDetachedMessage } from "./sharedSigner";

const NEP413_TAG = 2147484061;
const DEFAULT_RECIPIENT = "idos.network";

const nep413Schema = {
  struct: {
    tag: "u32",
    message: "string",
    nonce: { array: { type: "u8", len: 32 } },
    recipient: "string",
    callbackUrl: { option: "string" },
  },
} as const;

function createNonce(): Uint8Array {
  return crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
}

async function sha256(message: Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", message);
  return new Uint8Array(hash);
}

export function nearPublicKeyFromBytes(publicKey: Uint8Array): string {
  return `ed25519:${bs58.encode(publicKey)}`;
}

export function implicitNearAddress(publicKey: Uint8Array): string {
  return Array.from(publicKey, (byte) => byte.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
}

export async function signNearMessage({
  privateKeyBase64,
  message,
  recipient = DEFAULT_RECIPIENT,
}: {
  privateKeyBase64: string;
  message: string;
  recipient?: string;
}): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const nonce = createNonce();
  const payload = serialize(nep413Schema, {
    tag: NEP413_TAG,
    message,
    nonce: Array.from(nonce),
    recipient,
    callbackUrl: null,
  });
  const digest = await sha256(payload);
  const signature = signDetachedMessage(privateKeyBase64, digest);

  return concatBytes(uint16ToBigEndian(payload.length), payload, signature);
}

import { serialize, deserialize } from 'borsh';
import bs58 from 'bs58';
import nacl from 'tweetnacl';

const schema = {
  struct: {
    tag: 'u32',
    message: 'string',
    nonce: { array: { type: 'u8', len: 32 } },
    recipient: 'string',
    callbackUrl: { option: 'string' },
  },
};

const keyPair = nacl.sign.keyPair();
const message = 'Link this generated Canton signer to my idOS profile';
const nonce = new Uint8Array(32).map((_, i) => i);
const payload = serialize(schema, {
  tag: 2147484061,
  message,
  nonce: Array.from(nonce),
  recipient: 'idos.network',
  callbackUrl: null,
});
const digest = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', payload.buffer.slice(payload.byteOffset, payload.byteOffset + payload.byteLength)));
const signature = nacl.sign.detached(digest, keyPair.secretKey);
const packed = new Uint8Array(2 + payload.length + signature.length);
packed[0] = (payload.length >> 8) & 0xff;
packed[1] = payload.length & 0xff;
packed.set(payload, 2);
packed.set(signature, 2 + payload.length);

const payloadLength = new DataView(packed.buffer).getUint16(0, false);
const payloadBytes = packed.slice(2, 2 + payloadLength);
const actualSignature = packed.slice(2 + payloadLength);
const deserialized = deserialize(schema, payloadBytes);
const reconstructed = serialize(schema, {
  tag: 2147484061,
  message,
  nonce: deserialized.nonce,
  recipient: deserialized.recipient,
  callbackUrl: deserialized.callbackUrl,
});
const reconstructedHash = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', reconstructed.buffer.slice(reconstructed.byteOffset, reconstructed.byteOffset + reconstructed.byteLength)));
const ok = nacl.sign.detached.verify(reconstructedHash, actualSignature, keyPair.publicKey);
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  nearPublicKey: `ed25519:${bs58.encode(keyPair.publicKey)}`,
  implicitAddress: Buffer.from(keyPair.publicKey).toString('hex'),
  payloadLength,
  verified: ok,
}));

createSignerRecord() : (readStoredSigner() ?? createSignerRecord());\n  persistSigner(record);\n\n  const cantonPublicKeyBase64 = getPublicKeyFromPrivate(record.privateKeyBase64);\n  const publicKeyBytes = base64ToBytes(cantonPublicKeyBase64);\n  const ed25519PublicKeyHex = bytesToHex(publicKeyBytes);\n  const nearPublicKey = nearPublicKeyFromBytes(publicKeyBytes);\n  const idosSignatureBytes = await signNearMessage({\n    privateKeyBase64: record.privateKeyBase64,\n    message: SAMPLE_IDOS_MESSAGE,\n  });\n\n  return {\n    privateKeyBase64: record.privateKeyBase64,\n    cantonPublicKeyBase64,\n    ed25519PublicKeyHex,\n    idosAdapter: {\n      publicAddress: implicitNearAddress(publicKeyBytes),\n      publicKey: nearPublicKey,\n      signatureType: \"nep413\",\n      walletType: \"NEAR\",\n    },\n    sample: {\n      cantonHashHex: SAMPLE_CANTON_HASH,\n      cantonSignatureBase64: signTransactionHash(SAMPLE_CANTON_HASH, record.privateKeyBase64),\n      idosMessage: SAMPLE_IDOS_MESSAGE,\n      idosSignatureHex: bytesToHex(idosSignatureBytes),\n    },\n  };\n}\n",

## Assistant

The Wallet SDK keeps the fingerprint behind its initialized namespace, which is heavier than we need. I’m checking whether the underlying signing library already gives us the two primitives we care about directly: signature verification and, if possible, a stable fingerprint derivation without needing a live Canton provider.

Rather than invent a fake Canton fingerprint, I’m going to expose the verified transaction-hash roundtrip and label the base64 public key as the Canton signing key. That keeps the claim precise and avoids pretending we computed a participant-side fingerprint we didn’t.

function verifyCantonTransactionHash(
  transactionHashBase64: string,
  publicKeyBase64: string,
  signatureBase64: string,
): boolean {
  return nacl.sign.detached.verify(
    base64ToBytes(transactionHashBase64),
    base64ToBytes(signatureBase64),
    base64ToBytes(publicKeyBase64),
  );

# experiment-canton

PoC for sharing a single Ed25519 signer between:

- Canton external-party signing primitives
- idOS user authentication

The current repo avoids Daml and Canton account abstraction on purpose. The focus is signer reuse.

## Current status

Working today:

- generate and persist one browser-local Ed25519 keypair
- derive a Canton signing key view from that keypair
- sign and verify a Canton-style transaction hash roundtrip
- derive a `NEAR` wallet view for idOS from that same keypair
- link that generated signer to an existing idOS profile
- authenticate to idOS using the generated signer after linking

## Stack

- Vite
- React
- TypeScript
- `@canton-network/wallet-sdk`
- `@kwilteam/kwil-js`
- browser-side `tweetnacl`

## Run locally

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Then open the local Vite URL in a browser with an injected EVM wallet.

## Happy path

1. Open the app.
2. Let it create or load the shared signer from browser storage.
3. Connect an existing EVM wallet that already has an idOS profile.
4. Click `Link generated signer as NEAR wallet`.
5. After linking succeeds, click `Authenticate generated signer`.

Expected result:

- the generated signer shows `Has profile: true`
- the generated signer shows `Wallet visible: true`
- the idOS user id resolves through the generated signer session

## Important implementation detail

The generated signer is linked to idOS as:

- `wallet_type: "NEAR"`
- `address`: NEAR implicit address derived from the Ed25519 public key
- `public_key`: `ed25519:<base58>`

The proof used for idOS is a browser-generated NEP-413 signature. This kept the integration simpler than trying to force the key through FaceSign-specific flows.

## Files worth reading

- [src/lib/sharedSigner.ts](src/lib/sharedSigner.ts)
  Shared Ed25519 key lifecycle plus Canton/idOS views of the same key
- [src/lib/near.ts](src/lib/near.ts)
  NEP-413 message construction and signing
- [src/lib/idos/client.ts](src/lib/idos/client.ts)
  Thin idOS-specific client logic for profile inspection and wallet linking
- [src/App.tsx](src/App.tsx)
  Demo UI and browser flow

## Validation used so far

- `pnpm build`
- direct reachability checks against `https://nodes.idos.network`
- local NEP-413 packing and verification sanity checks
- browser validation with a real idOS profile

## Known limits

- No Daml code
- No Canton network write path yet
- No Canton external-party allocation flow yet
- No MPC-specific wallet sync work
- The generated key is stored in browser `localStorage`
- Bundle size is large because the current app pulls the Canton SDK into the browser bundle

## Next likely steps

- replace the sample Canton signing panel with a more explicit external-party preparation flow
- decide whether a real Canton provider should be added to the demo
- reduce bundle size by code-splitting or moving some Canton logic off the initial client path

## Assistant

Yes. I would not block on Console Wallet.

For this experiment, the best move is actually to use no third-party wallet at all on the Canton side. Digital Asset’s DevNet docs are centered on the external-party flow: create an external party, prepare a transaction, sign the hash externally, and submit it. That lines up almost perfectly with what we already proved on the idOS side: one shared Ed25519 signer, two adapters. I also checked the installed `@canton-network/wallet-sdk` package in this repo, and its README says it currently supports `NodeJS` environments, so the practical shape is a tiny local Node bridge for Canton DevNet, not a browser wallet.

If you still want a wallet fallback, `Nightly` is the best current candidate I found. Canton’s ecosystem site lists it as a wallet, and Nightly publishes Canton-specific docs for connect/sign/RPC plus a public extension download page. `5N Loop` also looks public and browser-based, but I couldn’t verify its DevNet story from the docs I could access, so I’d rank it behind Nightly.

My recommendation is:
1. Don’t wait on the whitelist.
2. I pivot the next loop to a local Canton DevNet bridge using the official external-party SDK.
3. If we later want a wallet-based demo too, we try Nightly first.

If you want, I’ll take that path now and start wiring the Canton side without any wallet dependency.

  "stdout": "# Wallet Auth\n\nThis workspace contains the authentication logic and interfaces used by the Wallet Gateway.\nIt provides abstractions for authentication services, user identity management, and integration points for different identity providers (IDPs), such as password-based and OAuth2/OIDC-based authentication.\n\n## Installation\n\nThis package requires [NodeJS](https://nodejs.org/) v16 or higher and can be added to your project using:\n\n```sh\nnpm install @canton-network/core-wallet-auth --save\n```\n\nor\n\n```sh\nyarn add @canton-network/core-wallet-auth\n```\n\n## Interfaces\n\nThis workspace defines several core interfaces for authentication.\n\n### [AuthContext](./src/AuthService.ts)\n\nRepresents the authentication context for a user, including their unique user ID and the associated access token.\n\n### [AuthAware](./src/AuthService.ts)\n\nProvides a pattern for classes or services that are aware of const DEFAULT_PORT = 8787;
const LOCALNET_AUTH = {
  method: "self_signed",
  issuer: "unsafe-auth",
  audience: "https://canton.network.global",
  scope: "",
  clientId: localNetStaticConfig.LOCALNET_USER_ID,
  clientSecret: "unsafe",
};

let sdkPromise;

function readEnv(name) {
  const value = process.env[name]?.trim();

  return value ? value : undefined;
}

function parsePort(value) {
  const parsed = Number.parseInt(value ?? "", 10);

  return Number.isInteger(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : DEFAULT_PORT;
}

function buildConfiguredBridgeConfig(overrides) {
  return {
    configured: true,
    missingFields: [],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function loadBridgeConfig() {
  const network = readEnv("CANTON_NETWORK") ?? "unconfigured";
  const port = parsePort(readEnv("CANTON_BRIDGE_PORT"));

  if (network === "localnet") {
    return {
      port,
      ...buildConfiguredBridgeConfig({
        network,
        ledgerClientUrl: localNetStaticConfig.LOCALNET_APP_USER_LEDGER_URL.toString(),
        auth: LOCALNET_AUTH,
      }),
    };
  }

  if (network === "devnet" || network === "custom") {
    const requiredEnvNames = [
      "CANTON_LEDGER_CLIENT_URL",
      "CANTON_AUTH_ISSUER",
      "CANTON_AUTH_AUDIENCE",
      "CANTON_AUTH_CLIENT_ID",
      "CANTON_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET",
    ];
    const missingFields = requiredEnvNames.filter((name) => !readEnv(name));

    return {
      port,
      configured: missingFields.length === 0,
      missingFields,
      network,
      ledgerClientUrl: readEnv("CANTON_LEDGER_CLIENT_URL") ?? null,
      auth:
        missingFields.length === 0
          ? {
              method: "self_signed",
              issuer: readEnv("CANTON_AUTH_ISSUER"),
              audience: readEnv("CANTON_AUTH_AUDIENCE"),
              scope: readEnv("CANTON_AUTH_SCOPE") ?? "",
              clientId: readEnv("CANTON_AUTH_CLIENT_ID"),
              clientSecret: readEnv("CANTON_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET"),
            }
          : null,
    };
  }

  return {
    port,
    configured: false,
    missingFields: ["CANTON_NETWORK"],
    network,
    ledgerClientUrl: null,
    auth: null,
  };
}

function toPublicHealth(config) {
  return {
    ok: true,
    bridge: "canton",
    version: 1,
    network: config.network,
    configured: config.configured,
    ledgerClientUrl: config.ledgerClientUrl,
    authMethod: config.auth?.method ?? null,
    issuer: config.auth?.issuer ?? null,
    audience: config.auth?.audience ?? null,
    clientId: config.auth?.clientId ?? null,
    missingFields: config.missingFields,
  };
}

function writeJson(response, statusCode, payload) {
  response.writeHead(statusCode, {
    "access-control-allow-origin": "*",
    "access-control-allow-methods": "GET,POST,OPTIONS",
    "access-control-allow-headers": "content-type",
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
  });
  response.end(JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2));
}

function writeNoContent(response) {
  response.writeHead(204, {
    "access-control-allow-origin": "*",
    "access-control-allow-methods": "GET,POST,OPTIONS",
    "access-control-allow-headers": "content-type",
  });
  response.end();
}

function readRequestBody(request) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let raw = "";

    request.setEncoding("utf8");
    request.on("data", (chunk) => {
      raw += chunk;
    });
    request.on("end", () => {
      if (!raw) {
        resolve({});
        return;
      }

      try {
        resolve(JSON.parse(raw));
      } catch (error) {
        reject(new Error("Request body must be valid JSON."));
      }
    });
    request.on("error", reject);
  });
}

async function getSdk(config) {
  if (!config.configured || !config.auth || !config.ledgerClientUrl) {
    throw new Error("Canton bridge is not configured yet.");
  }

  if (!sdkPromise) {
    sdkPromise = SDK.create({
      auth: config.auth,
      ledgerClientUrl: config.ledgerClientUrl,
      logAdapter: "console",
    }).catch((error) => {
      sdkPromise = undefined;
      throw error;
    });
  }

  return sdkPromise;
}

async function handlePrepareTopology(request, response) {
  const config = loadBridgeConfig();

  if (!config.configured) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "Canton bridge is not configured.",
      missingFields: config.missingFields,
    });
    return;
  }

  const payload = await readRequestBody(request);
  const publicKeyBase64 =
    typeof payload.publicKeyBase64 === "string" ? payload.publicKeyBase64.trim() : "";
  const partyHint = typeof payload.partyHint === "string" ? payload.partyHint.trim() : "";

  if (!publicKeyBase64) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "`publicKeyBase64` is required.",
    });
    return;
  }

  const sdk = await getSdk(config);
  const prepared = sdk.party.external.create(
    publicKeyBase64,
    partyHint ? { partyHint } : undefined,
  );
  const topology = await prepared.topology();

  writeJson(response, 200, {
    ok: true,
    topology,
  });
}

const server = createServer(async (request, response) => {
  const method = request.method ?? "GET";
  const url = new URL(request.url ?? "/", `http://${request.headers.host ?? "127.0.0.1"}`);

  if (method === "OPTIONS") {
    writeNoContent(response);
    return;
  }

  try {
    if (method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/healthz") {
      writeJson(response, 200, toPublicHealth(loadBridgeConfig()));
      return;
    }

    if (method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/v1/external-party/topology") {
      await handlePrepareTopology(request, response);
      return;
    }

    writeJson(response, 404, {
      ok: false,
      error: "Route not found.",
    });
  } catch (error) {
    writeJson(response, 500, {
      ok: false,
      error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unexpected bridge error.",
    });
  }
});

const { port } = loadBridgeConfig();

server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => {
  console.log(`Canton bridge listening on http://127.0.0.1:${port}`);
});

```

const DEFAULT_CANTON_BRIDGE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8787";

export type CantonBridgeHealth = {
  ok: boolean;
  bridge: "canton";
  version: number;
  network: string;
  configured: boolean;
  ledgerClientUrl: string | null;
  authMethod: string | null;
  issuer: string | null;
  audience: string | null;
  clientId: string | null;
  missingFields: string[];
};

export function getCantonBridgeUrl(): string {
  const configuredUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_CANTON_BRIDGE_URL;

  return typeof configuredUrl === "string" && configuredUrl.trim()
    ? configuredUrl.trim()
    : DEFAULT_CANTON_BRIDGE_URL;
}

export async function probeCantonBridge(): Promise<CantonBridgeHealth> {
  const response = await fetch(`${getCantonBridgeUrl()}/healthz`);

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Canton bridge probe failed with status ${response.status}.`);
  }

  return (await response.json()) as CantonBridgeHealth;
}

## Canton bridge

The browser app does not talk to the Canton SDK directly for the real network path anymore.
Instead it expects a small local bridge process:

- `GET /healthz`
  Returns bridge config status for the UI
- `POST /v1/external-party/topology`
  Accepts a Canton public key and returns prepared external-party topology plus the `multiHash` that the browser signer should sign

Bridge configuration is env-driven:

- `CANTON_NETWORK=localnet`
  Uses the documented LocalNet defaults plus the standard unsafe self-signed auth
- `CANTON_NETWORK=devnet` or `custom`
  Requires your own validator ledger API URL and self-signed auth env vars

There is an `.env.example` file with the supported variables.

export async function prepareCantonExternalPartyTopology(input: {
  partyHint?: string;
  publicKeyBase64: string;
}): Promise<CantonPreparedTopology> {
  const response = await fetch(`${getCantonBridgeUrl()}/v1/external-party/topology`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "content-type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(input),
  });
  const payload = (await response.json()) as
    | { error?: string; ok: false }
    | { ok: true; topology: CantonPreparedTopology };

  if (!response.ok || !payload.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      ("error" in payload && payload.error) || "Failed to prepare Canton external-party topology.",
    );
  }

  return payload.topology;
}

async function handleAllocateParty(request, response) {
  const config = loadBridgeConfig();

  if (!config.configured) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "Canton bridge is not configured.",
      missingFields: config.missingFields,
    });
    return;
  }

  const payload = await readRequestBody(request);
  const body =
    payload && typeof payload === "object" && !Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : {};
  const publicKeyBase64 =
    typeof body.publicKeyBase64 === "string" ? body.publicKeyBase64.trim() : "";
  const partyHint = typeof body.partyHint === "string" ? body.partyHint.trim() : "";
  const signature = typeof body.signature === "string" ? body.signature.trim() : "";

  if (!publicKeyBase64 || !signature) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "`publicKeyBase64` and `signature` are required.",
    });
    return;
  }

  const sdk = await getSdk(config);
  const prepared = sdk.party.external.create(
    publicKeyBase64,
    partyHint ? { partyHint } : undefined,
  );
  const allocation = await prepared.execute(signature);

  writeJson(response, 200, {
    ok: true,
    allocation,
  });
}

export async function allocateCantonExternalParty(input: {
  partyHint?: string;
  publicKeyBase64: string;
  signature: string;
}): Promise<CantonAllocatedParty> {
  const response = await fetch(`${getCantonBridgeUrl()}/v1/external-party/allocate`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "content-type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(input),
  });
  const payload = (await response.json()) as
    | { allocation?: CantonAllocatedParty; error?: string; ok: false }
    | { allocation: CantonAllocatedParty; ok: true };

  if (!response.ok || !payload.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      ("error" in payload && payload.error) || "Failed to allocate the Canton external party.",
    );
  }

  return payload.allocation;
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
WORK_ROOT="${CANTON_LOCALNET_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/.local/canton-localnet}"
DOWNLOADS_DIR="$WORK_ROOT/downloads"
RELEASES_DIR="$WORK_ROOT/releases"
LATEST_RELEASE_API="https://api.github.com/repos/digital-asset/decentralized-canton-sync/releases/latest"
ACTION="${1:-doctor}"
TARGET_VERSION="${CANTON_LOCALNET_VERSION:-}"
DRY_RUN="${CANTON_LOCALNET_DRY_RUN:-0}"

RELEASE_VERSION=""
RELEASE_TAG=""
RELEASE_ASSET_URL=""
TARBALL_PATH=""
EXTRACT_DIR=""
LOCALNET_DIR=""
COMPOSE_ENV_FILE=""
COMMON_ENV_FILE=""
COMPOSE_FILE=""
RESOURCE_FILE=""
COMPOSE_BIN=()

run() {
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]]; then
    printf '+'
    for arg in "$@"; do
      printf ' %q' "$arg"
    done
    printf '\n'
    return 0
  fi

  "$@"
}

require_tool() {
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'Missing required tool: %s\n' "$1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

detect_compose() {
  if command -v podman-compose >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    COMPOSE_BIN=(podman-compose)
    return
  fi

  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1 && podman compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    COMPOSE_BIN=(podman compose)
    return
  fi

  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    COMPOSE_BIN=(docker compose)
    return
  fi

  printf 'No supported compose engine found. Install podman-compose, podman compose, or docker compose.\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

release_metadata_json() {
  if [[ -n "$TARGET_VERSION" ]]; then
    curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/digital-asset/decentralized-canton-sync/releases/tags/v${TARGET_VERSION#v}"
    return
  fi

  curl -fsSL "$LATEST_RELEASE_API"
}

resolve_release() {
  require_tool curl
  require_tool jq

  local release_json asset_name

  release_json="$(release_metadata_json)"
  RELEASE_TAG="$(printf '%s' "$release_json" | jq -r '.tag_name')"
  RELEASE_VERSION="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"
  asset_name="${RELEASE_VERSION}_splice-node.tar.gz"
  RELEASE_ASSET_URL="$(printf '%s' "$release_json" | jq -r --arg asset_name "$asset_name" '.assets[] | select(.name == $asset_name) | .browser_download_url')"

  if [[ -z "$RELEASE_ASSET_URL" || "$RELEASE_ASSET_URL" == "null" ]]; then
    printf 'Could not resolve splice-node asset for release %s.\n' "$RELEASE_TAG" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  TARBALL_PATH="$DOWNLOADS_DIR/$asset_name"
  EXTRACT_DIR="$RELEASES_DIR/$RELEASE_VERSION"
  LOCALNET_DIR="$EXTRACT_DIR/splice-node/docker-compose/localnet"
  COMPOSE_ENV_FILE="$LOCALNET_DIR/compose.env"
  COMMON_ENV_FILE="$LOCALNET_DIR/env/common.env"
  COMPOSE_FILE="$LOCALNET_DIR/compose.yaml"
  RESOURCE_FILE="$LOCALNET_DIR/resource-constraints.yaml"
}

ensure_bundle() {
  require_tool tar
  mkdir -p "$DOWNLOADS_DIR" "$RELEASES_DIR"

  if [[ -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ]]; then
    return
  fi

  if [[ ! -f "$TARBALL_PATH" ]]; then
    run curl -fL "$RELEASE_ASSET_URL" -o "$TARBALL_PATH"
  fi

  mkdir -p "$EXTRACT_DIR"
  run tar -xzf "$TARBALL_PATH" -C "$EXTRACT_DIR"
}

compose_base_args() {
  printf '%s\0' \
    --env-file "$COMPOSE_ENV_FILE" \
    --env-file "$COMMON_ENV_FILE" \
    -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" \
    -f "$RESOURCE_FILE" \
    --profile sv \
    --profile app-provider \
    --profile app-user
}

compose_with_base() {
  local args=()

  while IFS= read -r -d '' arg; do
    args+=("$arg")
  done < <(compose_base_args)

  run "${COMPOSE_BIN[@]}" "${args[@]}" "$@"
}

doctor() {
  detect_compose
  resolve_release

  printf 'Compose engine: %s\n' "${COMPOSE_BIN[*]}"
  printf 'Release tag: %s\n' "$RELEASE_TAG"
  printf 'Bundle URL: %s\n' "$RELEASE_ASSET_URL"
  printf 'Work root: %s\n' "$WORK_ROOT"
  printf 'Bundle path: %s\n' "$TARBALL_PATH"
  printf 'Extract dir: %s\n' "$EXTRACT_DIR"
  printf 'LocalNet dir: %s\n' "$LOCALNET_DIR"

  if [[ -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ]]; then
    printf 'Bundle status: extracted\n'
  elif [[ -f "$TARBALL_PATH" ]]; then
    printf 'Bundle status: downloaded\n'
  else
    printf 'Bundle status: missing\n'
  fi

  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if podman info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf 'Podman status: ready\n'
    else
      printf 'Podman status: unavailable\n'
    fi
  fi
}

up() {
  detect_compose
  resolve_release
  ensure_bundle
  compose_with_base up -d
}

down() {
  detect_compose
  resolve_release

  if [[ ! -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ]]; then
    printf 'LocalNet bundle is not extracted yet. Nothing to stop.\n'
    return
  fi

  compose_with_base down -v
}

ps_cmd() {
  detect_compose
  resolve_release
  ensure_bundle
  compose_with_base ps
}

logs_cmd() {
  detect_compose
  resolve_release
  ensure_bundle
  shift || true
  compose_with_base logs -f "$@"
}

env_cmd() {
  resolve_release

  cat <<EOF
export LOCALNET_DIR="$LOCALNET_DIR"
export IMAGE_TAG="$RELEASE_VERSION"
EOF
}

download_cmd() {
  resolve_release
  ensure_bundle
  printf 'Bundle ready at %s\n' "$LOCALNET_DIR"
}

case "$ACTION" in
  doctor)
    doctor
    ;;
  download)
    download_cmd
    ;;
  env)
    env_cmd
    ;;
  up)
    up
    ;;
  down)
    down
    ;;
  ps)
    ps_cmd
    ;;
  logs)
    logs_cmd "$@"
    ;;
  *)
    cat <<'EOF' >&2
Usage: scripts/canton-localnet.sh [doctor|download|env|up|down|ps|logs]

Environment:
  CANTON_LOCALNET_VERSION   Override the Splice release version. Example: 0.5.18
  CANTON_LOCALNET_ROOT      Override the local bundle cache directory
  CANTON_LOCALNET_DRY_RUN   Set to 1 to print commands without executing them
EOF
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

```

## LocalNet bootstrap

The repo now includes a LocalNet wrapper around the official Splice compose bundle:

```bash
pnpm canton:localnet:doctor
pnpm canton:localnet:download
pnpm canton:localnet:up
pnpm canton:bridge:localnet
```

Notes:

- the wrapper prefers `podman-compose`
- it falls back to `podman compose` and then `docker compose`
- LocalNet artifacts are cached under `.local/canton-localnet`
- the bundle version is resolved from the latest Digital Asset `decentralized-canton-sync` release unless `CANTON_LOCALNET_VERSION` is set

The wrapper script lives at [scripts/canton-localnet.sh](scripts/canton-localnet.sh).

## User (checkpoint)

I found two separate problems.

The host-side `podman machine` path on this Mac is broken: Podman 5.8.2 on macOS 26.4.1 boots the `applehv` VM but never completes the ready handshake. The working backend here is the existing Lima VM, so for raw Podman commands the safe form is `CONTAINER_CONNECTION=lima-podman podman ...`.

In the repo, I patched [scripts/canton-localnet.sh](/Users/pkoch/github.com/idos-network/experiment-canton/scripts/canton-localnet.sh) so the LocalNet wrapper works with `podman-compose` instead of tripping over the upstream bundle. The script now exports the compose defaults Podman was missing, renders a Podman-safe compose file with resolved port mappings, and fully qualifies short-name images. After that:
- `pnpm canton:localnet:doctor` reports `Podman status: ready`
- `bash scripts/canton-localnet.sh ps` no longer dies on `PARTY_HINT`
- `pnpm canton:localnet:up` now gets past compose parsing and starts containers under Podman

Current runtime state from the smoke test: `postgres` and `canton` are healthy, `splice` is up and answering on `:2903`, and `nginx` is waiting for `splice`’s healthcheck to flip before it starts. If you want to inspect or stop it, use `bash scripts/canton-localnet.sh ps` and `pnpm canton:localnet:down`.

import { signTransactionHash, getPublicKeyFromPrivate } from '@canton-network/wallet-sdk';

const keyPair = nacl.sign.keyPair();

const publicKeyBase64 = getPublicKeyFromPrivate(privateKeyBase64);
const partyHint = `idos-shared-${Date.now()}`;

const topologyResponse = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/external-party/topology', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ publicKeyBase64, partyHint }),
});
const topologyPayload = await topologyResponse.json();
console.log(JSON.stringify({ step: 'topology', status: topologyResponse.status, payload: topologyPayload }, null, 2));
if (!topologyResponse.ok || !topologyPayload.ok) process.exit(1);

const signature = signTransactionHash(topologyPayload.topology.multiHash, privateKeyBase64);
const allocationResponse = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/external-party/allocate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ publicKeyBase64, partyHint, signature }),
});
const allocationPayload = await allocationResponse.json();
console.log(JSON.stringify({ step: 'allocation', status: allocationResponse.status, payload: allocationPayload }, null, 2));

import nacl from "tweetnacl";
import { getPublicKeyFromPrivate, signTransactionHash } from "@canton-network/wallet-sdk";

const bridgeUrl = process.env.CANTON_BRIDGE_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:8787";
const partyHint = process.env.CANTON_PARTY_HINT ?? `idos-shared-${Date.now()}`;

async function postJson(path, payload) {
  const response = await fetch(`${bridgeUrl}${path}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "content-type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });
  const body = await response.json();

  if (!response.ok || !body.ok) {
    throw new Error(body.error ?? `Request to ${path} failed with status ${response.status}.`);
  }

  return body;
}

const keyPair = nacl.sign.keyPair();
const privateKeyBase64 = Buffer.from(keyPair.secretKey).toString("base64");
const publicKeyBase64 = getPublicKeyFromPrivate(privateKeyBase64);

const topology = await postJson("/v1/external-party/topology", {
  partyHint,
  publicKeyBase64,
});

const signature = signTransactionHash(topology.topology.multiHash, privateKeyBase64);

const allocation = await postJson("/v1/external-party/allocate", {
  partyHint,
  publicKeyBase64,
  signature,
});

console.log(
  JSON.stringify(
    {
      bridgeUrl,
      partyHint,
      publicKeyBase64,
      topology: topology.topology,
      allocation: allocation.allocation,
    },
    null,
    2,
  ),
);

```

## Assistant

The SDK surface is simple enough for a first write: `utils.ping.create(...)` returns plain `CreateCommand`s, and `ledger.prepare` only needs `partyId` plus those commands. I’m probing whether a freshly allocated external party can ping itself; if that works, that’s the cleanest next Canton transaction.

**Tool Call: Run node - <<'NODE'
import nacl from 'tweetnacl';
import { SDK, getPublicKeyFromPrivate, signTransactionHash, localNetStaticConfig } from '@canton-network/wallet-sdk';

const auth = {
  method: 'self_signed',
  issuer: 'unsafe-auth',
  credentials: {
    audience: 'https://canton.network.global',
    scope: '',
    clientId: localNetStaticConfig.LOCALNET_USER_ID,
    clientSecret: 'unsafe',
  },
};

const sdk = await SDK.create({ auth, ledgerClientUrl: localNetStaticConfig.LOCALNET_APP_USER_LEDGER_URL.toString(), logAdapter: 'console' });

const keyPair = nacl.sign.keyPair();
const privateKeyBase64 = Buffer.from(keyPair.secretKey).toString('base64');
const publicKeyBase64 = getPublicKeyFromPrivate(privateKeyBase64);
const partyHint = `idos-ping-${Date.now()}`;

const preparedParty = sdk.party.external.create(publicKeyBase64, { partyHint });
const topology = await preparedParty.topology();
const partySignature = signTransactionHash(topology.multiHash, privateKeyBase64);
const allocation = await preparedParty.execute(partySignature);

const pingCommands = sdk.utils.ping.create([{ initiator: allocation.partyId, responder: allocation.partyId }]);
const preparedPing = sdk.ledger.prepare({ partyId: allocation.partyId, commands: pingCommands });
const preparedJson = await preparedPing.toJSON();
console.log(JSON.stringify({ step: 'preparedPing', partyId: allocation.partyId, prepared: preparedJson }, null, 2));
const pingSignature = signTransactionHash(preparedJson.response.preparedTransactionHash, privateKeyBase64);
const signedPing = sdk.ledger.fromSignature(preparedJson.response, pingSignature);
const executed = await sdk.ledger.execute(signedPing, { partyId: allocation.partyId });
console.log(JSON.stringify({ step: 'executed', executed }, null, 2));
NODE**

    estimationTimestamp: string;

export async function prepareCantonPing(input: {
  partyId: string;
  responderPartyId?: string;
  pingId?: string;
}): Promise<CantonPreparedPing> {
  const response = await fetch(`${getCantonBridgeUrl()}/v1/ping/prepare`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "content-type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(input),
  });
  const payload = (await response.json()) as
    | { error?: string; ok: false }
    | { ok: true; ping: CantonPreparedPing };

  if (!response.ok || !payload.ok) {
    throw new Error(("error" in payload && payload.error) || "Failed to prepare Canton ping.");
  }

  return payload.ping;
}

export async function executeCantonPing(input: {
  partyId: string;
  responderPartyId?: string;
  pingId: string;
  response: CantonPreparedLedgerResponse;
  signature: string;
}): Promise<CantonExecutedPing> {
  const response = await fetch(`${getCantonBridgeUrl()}/v1/ping/execute`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "content-type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(input),
  });
  const payload = (await response.json()) as
    | { error?: string; ok: false }
    | { ok: true; execution: CantonExecutedPing };

  if (!response.ok || !payload.ok) {
    throw new Error(("error" in payload && payload.error) || "Failed to execute Canton ping.");
  }

  return payload.execution;
}

async function handlePreparePing(request, response) {
  const config = loadBridgeConfig();

  if (!config.configured) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "Canton bridge is not configured.",
      missingFields: config.missingFields,
    });
    return;
  }

  const payload = await readRequestBody(request);
  const body =
    payload && typeof payload === "object" && !Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : {};
  const partyId = typeof body.partyId === "string" ? body.partyId.trim() : "";
  const responderPartyId =
    typeof body.responderPartyId === "string" && body.responderPartyId.trim()
      ? body.responderPartyId.trim()
      : partyId;
  const pingId =
    typeof body.pingId === "string" && body.pingId.trim()
      ? body.pingId.trim()
      : `ping-${Date.now()}`;

  if (!partyId) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "`partyId` is required.",
    });
    return;
  }

  const sdk = await getSdk(config);
  const commands = sdk.utils.ping.create([
    {
      id: pingId,
      initiator: partyId,
      responder: responderPartyId,
    },
  ]);
  const prepared = sdk.ledger.prepare({
    partyId,
    commands,
  });
  const preparedJson = await prepared.toJSON();

  writeJson(response, 200, {
    ok: true,
    ping: {
      partyId,
      responderPartyId,
      pingId,
      response: preparedJson.response,
    },
  });
}

async function handleExecutePing(request, response) {
  const config = loadBridgeConfig();

  if (!config.configured) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "Canton bridge is not configured.",
      missingFields: config.missingFields,
    });
    return;
  }

  const payload = await readRequestBody(request);
  const body =
    payload && typeof payload === "object" && !Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : {};
  const partyId = typeof body.partyId === "string" ? body.partyId.trim() : "";
  const responderPartyId =
    typeof body.responderPartyId === "string" && body.responderPartyId.trim()
      ? body.responderPartyId.trim()
      : partyId;
  const pingId = typeof body.pingId === "string" ? body.pingId.trim() : "";
  const signature = typeof body.signature === "string" ? body.signature.trim() : "";
  const prepareResponse =
    body.response && typeof body.response === "object" && !Array.isArray(body.response)
      ? body.response
      : null;

  if (!partyId || !pingId || !signature || !prepareResponse) {
    writeJson(response, 400, {
      ok: false,
      error: "`partyId`, `pingId`, `response`, and `signature` are required.",
    });
    return;
  }

  const sdk = await getSdk(config);
  const signed = sdk.ledger.fromSignature(prepareResponse, signature);
  const executed = await sdk.ledger.execute(signed, { partyId });

  writeJson(response, 200, {
    ok: true,
    execution: {
      partyId,
      responderPartyId,
      pingId,
      preparedTransactionHash: prepareResponse.preparedTransactionHash,
      updateId: executed.updateId,
      completionOffset: executed.completionOffset,
    },
  });
}

  async function handlePrepareCantonPing() {
    if (!cantonAllocationState.result) {
      return;
    }

    setCantonPingState({
      error: null,
      loading: true,
      result: null,
    });

    try {
      const result = await prepareCantonPing({
        partyId: cantonAllocationState.result.partyId,
      });

      setCantonPingState({
        error: null,
        loading: false,
        result,
      });
      setCantonPingSignature(null);
      setCantonPingExecutionState({
        error: null,
        loading: false,
        result: null,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      setCantonPingState({
        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Failed to prepare Canton ping.",
        loading: false,
        result: null,
      });
    }
  }

  function handleSignPreparedPing() {
    if (!snapshot || !cantonPingState.result) {
      return;
    }

    setCantonPingSignature(
      signCantonTransactionHash(
        snapshot.privateKeyBase64,
        cantonPingState.result.response.preparedTransactionHash,
      ),
    );
    setCantonPingExecutionState({
      error: null,
      loading: false,
      result: null,
    });
  }

  async function handleExecuteCantonPing() {
    if (!cantonPingState.result || !cantonPingSignature) {
      return;
    }

    setCantonPingExecutionState({
      error: null,
      loading: true,
      result: null,
    });

    try {
      const result = await executeCantonPing({
        partyId: cantonPingState.result.partyId,
        responderPartyId: cantonPingState.result.responderPartyId,
        pingId: cantonPingState.result.pingId,
        response: cantonPingState.result.response,
        signature: cantonPingSignature,
      });

      setCantonPingExecutionState({
        error: null,
        loading: false,
        result,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      setCantonPingExecutionState({
        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Failed to execute Canton ping.",
        loading: false,
        result: null,
      });
    }
  }
